title: Prove the first tensor-phase threshold for widths 2 through k (no κ)
body:
## Result

New package `research/consecutive-tensor-phase-threshold`. **Scoped analytical theorem with exact finite corroboration. No new κ.**

For unitaries A, B with ‖A^(⊗j) − B^(⊗j)‖ ≤ ε at every width j = 2..k, put a = asin(ε/2). Below a threshold ε*, the sharp bound is ‖A − B‖ ≤ 2 sin(a/k). At ε* it jumps:

| widths | ε* | value at ε* |
|---|---|---|
| 2, 3 (#5916) | 2 sin(π/5) | 2 sin(2π/5) |
| 2..4, 2..5 | 2 sin(2π/7) | 2 sin(3π/7) |
| 2..6, 2..7 | √3 | 2 sin(4π/9) |
| 2..k, k ≥ 8 | √3 | √3 |

Scalar unitaries attain every value in every dimension; the threshold includes equality. For every k ≥ 6 the jump stays at √3, because exp(2πi/3) passes every width test at that budget. So extra width tests beyond six cannot rule out phase aliasing for ε ≥ √3.

**Argument** (PROOF.md): the scalar reduction of #5916, then the width-two set splits into a near branch [0, α/k] and a far branch around 1/2. The width-three, four and six tests exclude the far branch below the threshold and pin it to the stated points at the threshold.

This is an original extension of #5916 (widths 2, 3, equal budgets) and #6330 (widths 2, 3, unequal budgets) to any consecutive set of widths.

## Evidence and reproduction

From the repository root, CPython 3.12.15, standard library only:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/consecutive-tensor-phase-threshold/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/consecutive-tensor-phase-threshold/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/consecutive-tensor-phase-threshold
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/consecutive-tensor-phase-threshold --check-source-history
```

All four pass locally. Each direct run takes under one second (0.7 s measured); the registered runner takes about 1.6 s and prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. The commit preflight prints `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` for 6 files at base `7c49fe32c`.

`verify.py` computes the exact sublevel set {φ ∈ [0, 1/2] : ‖jφ‖ ≤ α, j = 2..k} as rational intervals for k = 3..64. It checks the small branch at eight budgets below each threshold (down to α* − 2^-200), and the isolated jump point at the threshold. It also checks the pass/fail widths of the witnesses 1/3, 4/9, 3/7 and 2/5. Four controls fail as designed. The finite range backs up the written proof; the claim for every k rests on PROOF.md.

## Limitations

- The theorem stops at the first jump; the envelope above ε* is not derived.
- Non-consecutive width sets, unequal per-width budgets, projective comparisons and independently rounded factors are not covered.
- No caller application: `native_all_columns` and the other four framework assumptions keep their status. No physical precision, tape or storage cost is priced.
- No new κ, frontier change, supplier admission or complete multiplication theorem. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Envelope above the threshold. The next valleys of max_j ‖jφ‖ are at 4/11 (k = 8, 9), 5/13 (k = 10, 11) and 2/5 (k ≥ 12).
- First threshold for non-consecutive width sets or unequal per-width budgets (the arc-family method of #6330 applies).
- Bind an actual native-chart comparison to certified multi-width budgets.

## Related open work

No open PR studies the same quantity. #5549 (MatShep) concerns a Clifford tensor faithfulness width, which is a different question. Open PRs opened since the claim (#6652–#6662) study other objects; none computes this threshold.
